gen-dafont-true-north-gf-esteban: True North's middle band is so tall its lines look stocky, while Esteban keeps thin parts only slightly slimmer than its stems. Long paragraphs flow gently, its wide e never squeezing shut.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-faustina: Bowls thin gracefully rather than sharply, so the reading texture stays mild and approachable, with an open-jawed c. Faustina then lets True North's stocky, tall-bodied lines do the shouting above it.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-halant: Stubby and sturdy: Halant's towering x-height and outward-pointing terminals carry a faint thick-thin shift under True North's stocky lines. Both lean tall, so the headline and text feel cut from one block.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-headland-one: True North's middle band runs so tall that its lines look stocky, with curves that refuse to close. Headland One keeps letters well apart, so paragraph after paragraph never feels crowded.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-hedvig-letters-: True North's middle band is so tall its lines look stocky, while Hedvig Letters Serif leaves its curves open-ended. One shouts, the other speaks plainly, and both stand tall.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-marcellus-sc: Stocky meets stately: True North's tall middle band tightens each line while Marcellus SC pulls its terminals well back. And that gap in temperament, bold against dignified, is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-montagu-slab: Stocky up top: True North's tall middle band tightens the line, while Montagu Slab mixes robust downstrokes with slender turns. Its sizable x-height keeps long stretches of screen reading comfortable.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-noto-serif-hent: Noto Serif Hentaigana opens its jaws on every curved stroke. Its small letters rise nearly to capital height and its strokes modulate subtly, so paragraphs read steadily beneath True North's stocky headline.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-ovo: Ovo reads gently, its thins only slightly lighter than its thicks and its curve terminals spaced generously. And the tug between True North's stocky boldness and that softness is what makes it work.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-domine: Visitor's gaping e and short ascenders over big bowls give it a nostalgic, solder-drawn digital look. Domine adds compact ascenders and breathing room inside each curve, and that nostalgic-versus-dignified tension is the whole appeal.
